DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 77 s. 2021 10 June 2021 HON. BAI MARIAM SANGKI-MANGUDADATU Governor Maguindanao Dear Governor Sangki-Mangudadatu: This has reference to your letter dated 24 May 2021 requesting legal opinion as to the propriety of the actions of the Provincial Government of Maguindanao against that of the Ministry of Interior and Local Government (MILG), as represented by Minister Naguib G. Sinarimbo vis-å-vis the political impasse in the Municipality of Talitay, that province. Based on the documents forwarded to the Department, hereunder are the relevant factual antecedents: Vice-Mayor elect Montasir Sabal assumed the mayoralty post when his brother-elect Abdulwahab Sabal was gunned down in Manila last 10 February 2020; On 12 February 2020, Montasir Sabal was dismissed by the Supreme Court. The MILG BARMM was informed in letters dated 25 November 2020, 05 January 2021 and 08 January 2021; On 09 November 2020, Montasir Sabal relocated the entire municipal government in a private residence owned by deceased Abdulwahab Sabal without public consultation from the residents; Monaster Sabal filed his resignation on 04 March 2021, effective on 19 March 2021. The resignation was however accepted on 19 April 2021 ; You required the Vice-Mayor to take oath as Municipal Mayor; • First-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member-elect Moner K. Sabal assumed the mayoralty position by virtue of the Certificate of Recognition issued by the MILG dated 20 April 2021 ;

PNP Provincial Director issued Certification dated IO May 2021 that starting 22 March 2021, the mayor, vice-mayor and sangguniang bayan members of Talitay have not appeared for work, their absence resulted to the stoppage of government operations and services in the municipality; On 17 May 2021 , you installed caretaker officials in Talitay headed by the ABC President Fahad J. Midtimbang, on the basis of Sections 46, 47 and 465 (2) of the local Government Code since there is already abandonment of post on the part of the municipal elected officials; 0 18 May 2021, Provincial Administrator Mohajeran K. Balayman filed the case of misconduct in office, gross negligence, and dereliction of duty against all municipal elected officials; On 20 May 2021, despite due notice, the land Bank of the Philippines allowed the withdrawal of LGU Talitay based on the Certificate of Recognition issued by the MILG BARMM. Based on the aforesaid letter of Governor Mangudadatu, there are three (3) issues to be resolved by the Department, to wit: 1. Can the MILG allow the relocation of the government site to a privately owned land in Barangay Gadungan owned by deceased Mayor Abdulwahab Sabah without public consultation or hearing?; 2. Can you install a caretaker government since per certification issued by the PNP Provincial Director, the mayor, the vice-mayor and other LGU officials failed to appear for work since 22 March 3. Is the act of the MILG of recognizing all financial disbursement, transactions, communications and undertakings of Mayor Montasir Sabal proper? As to the first issue, may we invite your attention to Section 10, Article VI of Republic Act No. 11054 or the Organic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao reads:

"SEC. Bangsamoro Government and its Constituent Local Government Units.—The authority of the Bangsamoro Government to regulate the affairs of its constituent local government units shall be guaranteed in accordance with this Organic Law and a Bangsamoro local government code to be enacted by the Parliament. The privileges already enjoyed by local government units under Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the 'Local Government Code of 1991,' as amended, and other existing laws shall not be diminished. Xxxx (Emphasis Supplied) To this date however, BARMM has yet to enact their own local government code. For this, we deem it apt to invite your attention again to Section 4, Article XVI (Bangsamoro Transition Authority) of RA 11054, thus: "Section 4. Functions and Priorities. - The Bangsamoro Transition Authority shall ensure the accomplishment of the following prioritiesduring the transition period: (a) Enactment of priority legislations such as the Bangsamoro Administrative Code, Bangsamoro Revenue Code, Bangsamoro Electoral Code, Banqsamoro Local Government Code, and Bangsamoro Educational Code consistent with powers and prerogatives vested in the Bangsamoro Government by this Organic Law: Provided, That until the abovementioned laws are enacted. the Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 25. otherwise known as the "Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Local Government Code. " and subsisting laws on elections and other electoral matters shall apply in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region." (Emphasis Supplied) Section 11 of MMA 25 reads: "Sec. 11. Selection and Transfer of Local Government Site, Offices and Facilities. - (a) The law creating or merging local government units shall specify the seat of government from where governmental and corporate services shall be delivered. Provided, in selecting said site, factors relating to geographical centrality, accessibility, availability of transportation and communication facilities, drainage and sanitation, development and economic progress, and other relevant considerations shall be taken into account. (b)When conditions and develo ments in the local overnment unit chan ed subse uent to the concerned have si nificantl establishment of the seat of overnmen its san unian ma after ublic hearin and b a vote of two-thirds 213 of all its members transfer the same to a site better suited to its needs. Provided, however,

That no such transfer shall be made outside the territorial boundaries of the local government unit concerned. The old site, together with the improvements thereon, may be disposed of by sale or lease or converted to such other use as the sanggunian concerned may deem beneficial to the local government unit concerned and its inhabitants. (c) Local government offices and facilities shall not be transferred, relocated, or converted to other uses unless public hearings are first conducted for the purpose and the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the sanggunian concerned is obtained." Based on the aforequoted provision of the MMA 25 and in answer to the first issue, the seat of the government shall be transferred only after public hearing and by a vote of 2/3 of all the members of the Sangguniang Bayan of Talitay. The absence of these requisites means that the transfer of the seat of government is legally infirm. Subsequent recognition of such transfer of the seat of government by the MILG will not validate the same. As to the second issue, your designation and/or appointment of a caretaker government in Talitay, Maguindanao given the circumstances has already been discussed in the negative in a letter dated 20 May 2020 addressed to you. In the said letter, the Department opined that your appointment or designation of a caretaker is bereft of clear basis in law. The regulation of the affairs of constituent units in the BARMM region is governed by its Organic Law and a Bangsamoro Local Government Code. Unfortunately, the BOL is silent in the treatment of a situation where all the elected officials of a municipality are not performing their functions anymore. Also, the BARMM has yet to pass a Local Government Code where impasse of this nature can be addressed accordingly. Albeit as already discussed earlier, R.A. 11054 provides for the application of the Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 25, or the "Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Local Govemment Code," in the event that a Bangsamoro Local Government Code has not yet been enacted by the autonomous region, there is nothing therein which authorizes any person such as the Provincial Governor or the MILG to appoint or designate officials of a component municipality if all of its elective officials are no longer functional in view of their continuous absences from their offices. The absence or failure of the officials to report for work merely constitutes temporary vacancies where the rules on permanent vacancies under the Muslim Local Government Code of the erstwhile ARMM region are obviously inapplicable.

With regard to your reliance on Sections 46, 47 and 465 of R.A. 7160 as legal bases for installation of a caretaker government, the same is misplaced. As already explained, the LGC of 1991 cannot be used as basis of any actions in the autonomous region considering that Section 4, Article XVI of the Bangsamoro Organic Law has already settled the supplementary use of MMAA No. 25 in the event that no Bangsamoro Local Government Code has been enacted by the BARMM yet. This paralysis/hiatus in governance in Talitay, Maguidanao, however, should not be allowed to continue. Thus, this level submits that only the President can resolve this matter in view of his residual powers and the constitutional grant to him of the power of general supervision over local government units. Likewise, the BOL grants a similar power of oversight over the BARMM in favor of the President under Section 1, Article VI thereof.l As we have already provided in our first letter, an issuance from the President using his residual power under the Constitution and power of general supervision over the Bangsamoro Government to designate officials to fill-up the temporarily vacated offices in Talitay is in order. As to how the President will address this matter, he may perform the designation himself or delegate this function to the SILG or the MILG of the BARMM. A copy of said letter to you is hereto attached for ease of reference. As to the third issue, it is with much regret to inform you that we cannot competently answer the same given the limited facts stated in your letter. The dates and/or other circumstances when the alleged illegal financial disbursement, transactions, communications and undertakings made by Mayor Montasir Sabal were not indicated in the letter. Although it was stated that on 12 February 2020, Montasir Sabal was dismissed by the Supreme Court and meted the penalty of perpetual disqualification, we were not furnished a copy thereof. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BYT AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: US Loca L.
